title: Regasco cuts LPG prices by P2 a kilo today
teaser: 19 Filipino crew safe after tanker sinks, DMW eyes high-risk label for Black Sea, Job offer disguised as a vacation

sections.headline: Regasco cuts LPG by P2 a kilo
sections.body: Regasco, short for Republic Gas Corporation, cuts its LPG prices today, Thursday, November 19, by **P2 per kilogram**. A rollback is simply a price cut. Regasco president Arnel Ty said the move follows international contract prices, and he pointed to optimism over the peace talks between the United States and Iran. He also said more cuts are on the way this month: “‘Yan pong mga series of rollback this month of November ay tuloy-tuloy.” Regasco is not the first to cut. On November 3, Petron lowered its price by P3.74 per kilogram, and EC Gas and Pryce Gases by P4.00 per kilogram. Seaoil followed with P3.74 per kilogram on November 5. For the family at home, LPG is a regular kitchen expense, and since the cut is per kilo, bigger tanks see a bigger drop. What is still unknown is December: Ty said those prices will largely depend on end-of-November contract prices reported by Saudi Aramco. *GMA Money*: [Regasco to roll back LPG prices on Thursday, Nov. 19, 2026](https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/money/companies/1009960/regasco-to-roll-back-lpg-prices-on-thursday-nov-19-2026/story/)
sections.socialHook: Regasco cuts LPG prices by P2 per kilo starting today, and its president says more November rollbacks are coming.
sections.soWhat: If the family uses Regasco LPG, check the new price on your next refill; the cut is P2 per kilogram starting November 19.

sections.headline: 19 Filipino crew safe after tanker sinks
sections.body: All 19 Filipino seafarers aboard the LPG tanker Gas Husky were rescued after the ship sank off Bulgaria's Black Sea coast on Tuesday. The Liberian-flagged vessel was carrying 3,400 metric tons of LPG from Egypt to Romania when it sent a distress signal and went down about 50 miles east of Byala. Varna's regional governor, Mario Smarkov, said the ship took four strikes, though the sailors had not confirmed what kind of drones were used. Two maritime security sources told Reuters it was hit by an unmanned system. The Greece-based ship manager did not respond to a request for comment. The sinking came a day after a wheat carrier, the Betul 8, went down in the same area. Who is behind the attacks remains unconfirmed: Romanian and Bulgarian officials have been cautious about assigning blame, some experts suggest Russian involvement, and Moscow denies it. Still unknown is when the crew will fly home. *GMA Pinoy Abroad*: [LPG tanker with Filipinos onboard that sank off Bulgaria was hit by projectiles, official says](https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/pinoyabroad/dispatch/1009988/lpg-tanker-with-filipinos-onboard-that-sank-off-bulgaria-was-hit-by-projectiles-official-says/story/)

items.text: The first report, from Agence France Presse, has Bulgaria's defense ministry confirming the rescue and the ship's distress beacon going off at 8:02 am. *GMA Pinoy Abroad*: [LPG carrier with 19 Filipinos on board struck in Black Sea off Bulgaria; crew rescued](https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/pinoyabroad/dispatch/1009901/lpg-carrier-with-19-filipinos-on-board-struck-in-black-sea-off-bulgaria-crew-rescued/story/)

sections.socialHook: An LPG tanker sank off Bulgaria after reported drone strikes. All 19 Filipino crew members were rescued.
sections.soWhat: If a relative sails the Black Sea, keep the manning agency's contact details handy; DMW says it is working with the agency to bring this crew home.

sections.headline: DMW eyes high-risk label for Black Sea
sections.body: The Department of Migrant Workers (DMW) will recommend a review of whether the southwestern Black Sea, including waters near Bulgaria and Romania, should be classified as a high-risk or warlike zone. Migrant Workers Secretary Hans Leo Cacdac said the recent attacks show the danger now reaches beyond the areas already covered. Right now, the International Bargaining Forum (IBF) labels only parts of the Black Sea, including the northern region affected by the Russia-Ukraine war. This matters because seafarers in designated zones can get the right to refuse to sail, repatriation at the company's expense, extra pay and tighter security, depending on the label. Cacdac said two of the 19 Gas Husky crew had minor injuries, all survived, and they are in a hotel in Bulgaria where the labor attaché will visit. DMW is working with the DFA and the manning agency on their repatriation, meaning their trip home. Still unknown is whether and when the label will change, since the proposal still needs study. *GMA Pinoy Abroad*: [DMW mulls 'high-risk' label for southwestern Black Sea amid drone attacks](https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/pinoyabroad/dispatch/1009969/dmw-mulls-high-risk-label-for-southwestern-black-sea-amid-drone-attacks/story/)
sections.socialHook: DMW wants a review of whether the waters off Bulgaria and Romania should count as a high-risk zone for seafarers. Here is what that label would change.
sections.soWhat: The new label is not in effect yet; seafarer families can ask the manning agency which zone rules apply to the ship's route now.

sections.headline: Job offer disguised as a vacation
sections.body: The Bureau of Immigration (BI) says it stopped six Filipinos at NAIA Terminal 3 who were allegedly recruited for jobs in Armenia through a “deceptive travel scheme.” According to the BI, they arrived at the airport on November 6 saying they were going on a three-day vacation. We only have the report's summary, so other details are not confirmed here. The lesson for families is plain: a job abroad that asks you to leave as a tourist is a warning sign. Before paying any fee, check that the recruiter is licensed with the DMW. *Inquirer Global Nation*: [BI intercepts 6 Pinoys recruited through ‘deceptive’ job offers](https://globalnation.inquirer.net/348857/bi-intercepts-6-pinoys-recruited-through-deceptive-job-offers)
sections.socialHook: Six Filipinos were stopped at NAIA after allegedly being recruited for jobs abroad while posing as tourists. A real overseas job never starts that way.
sections.soWhat: If a recruiter says to travel as a tourist for a job abroad, stop and check the agency's license with DMW before paying anything.

sections.headline: Sabi nila

items.leadIn: PhilStar Opinion column (columnist not named in our material)
items.text: The writer argues that, away from the ASEAN Summit, the economy is weakening, pointing to slower growth, faster inflation and more Filipinos out of work. “Household spending, the main driver of the economy, is down to 2.8 percent.” *PhilStar Opinion*: [Marcos’ mismanaged economy](https://www.philstar.com/opinion/2026/11/18/2570800/marcos-mismanaged-economy)

sections.socialHook: One PhilStar columnist looks past the summit and writes about what slower spending and higher prices mean at home.

sections.headline: Iba pang balita

items.text: The peso weakened a little against the dollar on Wednesday. RCBC chief economist Michael Ricafort linked the dip to tensions between the US and Iran, but noted the peso has still posted a net gain over three weeks. *Manila Times Business*: [Peso weakens slightly against dollar](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/11/18/business/peso-weakens-slightly-against-dollar/2472845)

Foreign portfolio investments, called hot money because they can move in and out of the country quickly, had a net outflow of $488.53 million in September, 54.9 percent larger than in August, based on BSP data. *PhilStar Business*: [Hot money outflow widens to $489 million](https://www.philstar.com/business/2026/11/19/2571115/hot-money-outflow-widens-489-million)

The BI says it stopped a Vietnam-bound Filipino at NAIA Terminal 3 on November 7 after assessing the passenger as a potential victim of trafficking or illegal recruitment. Only the summary is available. *Inquirer Global Nation*: [BI stops Filipino passenger recruited for ‘job’ with foreign military](https://globalnation.inquirer.net/348803/bi-stops-filipino-passenger-recruited-for-job-with-foreign-military)

A report by identity-verification firm Sumsub found the Philippines accounted for 17 percent of the fraud networks it detected in Asia-Pacific, the largest number in the region. *Manila Times Business*: [PH tops Asia-Pacific in fraud networks](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/11/19/business/top-business/ph-tops-asia-pacific-in-fraud-networks/2473412)

sections.socialHook: Also this morning: the peso dips slightly, hot money leaves, and the Philippines tops a regional fraud report.
